source: NCERT Class XII, Politics in India Since Independence, Ch. 6 (The Crisis of Democratic Order).

sections.heading: 1. Background to the Emergency
points: In the early 1970s, India faced **economic crisis** (inflation, unemployment, poor monsoons, oil shock) and public discontent.
The **JP Movement (Jayaprakash Narayan)** — a mass movement in Bihar/Gujarat against corruption, calling for 'Total Revolution' and 'sampoorna kranti'.
The **Allahabad High Court (1975)** found Indira Gandhi guilty of electoral malpractice and declared her election void.

sections.heading: 2. Declaration of the Emergency (1975)
points: On **25 June 1975**, a **National Emergency** was declared (under **Article 352**), citing 'internal disturbance'.
President **Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed** proclaimed it on the advice of the government.
**Fundamental Rights were suspended**; press **censorship** imposed; opposition leaders **arrested (preventive detention)**.

sections.heading: 3. Emergency Rule and Excesses
points: The Emergency (1975–77) saw **curbs on civil liberties, press censorship, and arrests** of thousands.
**Excesses:** forced **sterilisation (family planning)** and **slum demolitions** (associated with Sanjay Gandhi) caused resentment.
The **42nd Amendment (1976)** made sweeping changes to the Constitution.
It was a major test of Indian democracy.

sections.heading: 4. End of Emergency and Its Lessons
points: In **1977**, elections were held; the Congress was **defeated**; the **Janata Party** (a coalition of opposition parties) came to power — the **first non-Congress government at the Centre (Morarji Desai PM)**.
The **44th Amendment (1978)** restored safeguards (e.g. 'internal disturbance' replaced by 'armed rebellion' for emergency; protected Articles 20, 21).
Lesson: the resilience of Indian democracy and the danger of concentration of power.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: JP Movement (Jayaprakash Narayan) = 'Total Revolution'.
Allahabad HC (1975) voided Indira Gandhi's election.
Emergency declared 25 June 1975 (Article 352, 'internal disturbance'); President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.
Emergency (1975–77): rights suspended, censorship, arrests; forced sterilisation.
1977 = Janata Party wins; first non-Congress government (Morarji Desai); 44th Amendment (1978) restored safeguards.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Emergency was declared on 25 June 1975** (under Article 352, 'internal disturbance').
The **JP Movement** was led by **Jayaprakash Narayan** ('Total Revolution').
The **1977 elections brought the Janata Party** (first non-Congress central government).
The **44th Amendment (1978)** restored democratic safeguards.
